solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The writer limited personal catastrophe

parts.note: the setter referring to themselves
the standard abbreviation for a limited company
one's own is one's personal property

explanation.surface: An author whose private disaster was kept small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The writer' is the setter's usual way of saying ME; 'limited' looks like an adjective on the writer but is the abbreviation LTD.
explanation.definitionFit: A meltdown, figuratively, is a sudden total collapse or disaster, whether financial, emotional or nuclear.

clue.text: Woman's work never done in this Notts town

parts.note: surface: the proverb that a woman's work is never done
setter's reading: the town's name splits as a man's area of work, the place where the woman's work is not done

explanation.surface: A weary housewife complaining about her endless chores in a Nottinghamshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the town as MAN'S FIELD: a field of work belonging to a man, so the woman's work is not done there. Notts is Nottinghamshire, an English Midlands county.
explanation.definitionFit: Mansfield is a market town in Nottinghamshire, north of the city of Nottingham.

clue.text: Guzzling girl due after draining coffee cups

indicators.note: to cup something is to hold it in the hands, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: a latte is a milky coffee

indicators.note: once something is drained its contents are gone, leaving only the outer shell of letters

parts.note: the word with its middle letter emptied out

explanation.surface: A girl gulping down her coffee because she's late.
explanation.walkthrough: LATTE opens to take DE: LA-DE-TTE. A ladette is British slang for a young woman who drinks heavily and behaves loutishly, like the lads.
explanation.definitionFit: The ladette of 1990s British culture was known for binge drinking, so a hard-drinking young woman fits well.

clue.text: Cavalryman dispatches one over fierce woman

indicators.note: to dispatch is to send away or kill, so a letter is got rid of

parts.note: a dragoon is a mounted soldier
O is the scorer's symbol for an over in cricket

explanation.surface: A mounted soldier sends a messenger over to a formidable woman.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the two Os in DRAGOON is removed; 'over' as O comes from cricket scorebooks.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling a woman a dragon is an idiom for a fierce, intimidating older woman, such as a stern aunt.

clue.text: Film director not last to capture old Siouan native

indicators.note: lacking its last means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Michael Winner, British director of Death Wish
to bag is to catch or capture
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A movie director who hasn't finished capturing an elderly Native American on film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capture' looks like an instruction to put one piece inside another, but it is simply BAG in a charade.
explanation.definitionFit: The Winnebago, or Ho-Chunk, are a Native American people whose language belongs to the Siouan family.

clue.text: Criminal snatching too much material

indicators.note: whatever is snatched is grabbed and held inside

parts.note: a con is a convict
OTT is over the top, excessive

explanation.surface: A thief grabbing an excessive amount of cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: CON takes OTT inside it; OTT, 'over the top', is a common British abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Cotton is a common fabric woven from the fibres around the seeds of the cotton plant.

clue.text: Wealthy man angry about EU split

indicators.note: about means around, so one set of letters goes round another

parts.note: cross means annoyed
taken as written, but its two letters are separated

explanation.surface: A rich man furious about the European Union splitting apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' tells you the E and U go into CROSS separately: CRO-E-S-U-S.
explanation.definitionFit: Croesus, a king of ancient Lydia, was so famously rich that his name became a byword for great wealth.

clue.text: Work to provide meaningful options in other words

definitions.text: Work to provide meaningful options in other words

parts.note: surface: a job or project offering worthwhile choices
setter's reading: a book offering alternatives with the same meaning, literally in other words

explanation.walkthrough: 'In other words' reads as a phrase meaning 'to put it differently', but literally the book offers choices of other words meaning the same thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a reference book listing synonyms, giving alternative words with the same or similar sense.

clue.text: Feature of city traffic in considerable volume

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the old full name of a bus
second meaning: a big book collecting several works

explanation.surface: Heavy congestion as a defining trait of urban roads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' suggests loudness or quantity of traffic; here it is a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus was originally called an omnibus, and an omnibus edition gathers several works into one large book.

clue.text: Retired lecturer gives green light

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw or go back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: An emeritus professor approves something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' looks like it describes the lecturer's career; it is the signal to read DON backwards. Don is the Oxbridge word for a university teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the nod means being given approval or permission, just like a green light to proceed.

clue.text: Perhaps ennoble any person finding royal favour at first

definitions.text: person finding royal favour at first

indicators.note: perhaps signals one possible version among many, so the letters can take another arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A king might raise anyone to the peerage who first wins his favour.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on history: she won Henry VIII's favour first and lost it, and her head, later.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry VIII's second wife enjoyed the king's affection initially before falling from grace and being executed in 1536.

clue.text: Perceived as carrying much weight in diamonds

parts.note: someone fat carries a lot of weight
at home means in, as in 'is he in?'
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Something seen as heavy with gems, perhaps a crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a linking preposition but is HOME, as in 'staying in'.
explanation.definitionFit: To fathom something is to understand it fully, so fathomed is a synonym for perceived or grasped.

clue.text: Despicable British bishop breaking silence, indeed

indicators.note: breaking into something means entering it, so letters push their way inside

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
ay is an old form of yes, indeed
B is the abbreviation for British
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A contemptible British churchman who broke his vow of silence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indeed' as AY is the old affirmative still heard in parliamentary votes ('the ayes have it'); the two Bs split the silence and the yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Shabby, of behaviour, means mean, unfair and contemptible, as in shabby treatment of a loyal employee.

clue.text: Bottom left corner unseen in country paradise

indicators.note: what is unseen is not there to be read, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a Scandinavian nation
on a map the bottom left is south-west

explanation.surface: A rural idyll where one corner of the map is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: On a compass-oriented map the bottom left corner is SW, which comes off the front of SWEDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garden of Eden in Genesis is the original paradise, and the name is used for any idyllic place.

clue.text: Local resident shows love for daughter in New Edinburgh

indicators.note: making something new means remaking it, so the letters take a fresh order
one thing for another means swapping it in as a replacement

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
D is the abbreviation for daughter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A local in Edinburgh displays affection for a girl in his family.
explanation.walkthrough: The D of EDINBURGH becomes O, giving EOINBURGH, which is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A neighbour is someone living nearby, the person next door or down the street.

clue.text: Question came up after lunatic returned plant

indicators.note: coming after places pieces in sequence, one following another
to return is to come back the way you went, so the letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: mad means insane
to question is to ask
rose means ascended

explanation.surface: A query arose once a madman brought back a houseplant.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads backwards: the reversed lunatic comes first, then the question, then came up.
explanation.definitionFit: The damask rose is a fragrant old garden rose species, grown for its oil and petals.

clue.text: Emerge bearing child close to natural philosopher

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so one piece holds others inside it

parts.note: to arise is to come up or appear
a tot is a small child

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone appearing carrying a baby, near a nature philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Natural philosopher' looks like one phrase, but only 'philosopher' defines; 'natural' is there to lend its closing letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle was the Greek thinker who studied under Plato and tutored Alexander the Great, one of philosophy's founding figures.

clue.text: Edited alert to include donation sent up after king

parts.note: ED is the abbreviation for edited

indicators.note: including something means taking it inside, so it goes within

parts.note: to alert is to warn

indicators.note: in a down clue sending something up makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: aid is help given

explanation.surface: A revised warning includes a gift sent upward, after a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edited' looks like an anagram signal but is ED. The definition means 'in the manner of, or following, King Edward'.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwardian describes the reign of Edward VII, 1901 to 1910, so it relates to or comes after that monarch.

clue.text: Musician involves keen crook in decline

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap up or enclose, so one piece takes others inside

parts.note: to die away is to decline
avid means eager
to bow is to bend or crook

explanation.surface: A performer gets an eager criminal mixed up in his downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' is not a criminal but the verb to bend, like a bow.
explanation.definitionFit: David Bowie was an English singer-songwriter and musician, famous for Ziggy Stardust and Heroes.

clue.text: Mister Solo animated after a little hesitation

indicators.note: coming after places one piece following another in sequence

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: animated means lively and moving about, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: er is a short sound of hesitation
taken as written

explanation.surface: Han Solo, or a man called Solo, coming to life after a brief pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mister' looks like a form of address but means a thing that produces mist.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosol can releases a fine spray, so it is literally something that mists.

clue.text: Mostly ambient musical combo

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: ambient music is typically without rhythm

explanation.surface: A band that plays largely atmospheric background music.
explanation.walkthrough: Ambient music often has no drum beat, so it is BEATLESS; take off its last S.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatles were the Liverpool four-piece band, a combo being an old word for a small group of musicians.

clue.text: Horse, observed outside wood

indicators.note: to be outside something is to surround it

parts.note: saw means noticed
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A horse seen at the edge of a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' wants to be the definition; it is drug slang for heroin, H.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw is an old and dialect word for a small wood or thicket, found in English place names.

clue.text: Motorbike was taken by husband? Nonsense!

parts.note: a hog is slang for a big motorcycle, especially a Harley
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Someone scoffing at the idea that the husband took the motorbike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken by' just places the husband after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogwash originally meant pig swill and now means worthless talk, a synonym of rubbish.

clue.text: Writer's block that's endless

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter goes

parts.note: a barrier blocks the way

explanation.surface: An author's creative blockage that never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer's block' reads as one phrase, but the writer is the definition and the block is a barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie was the Scottish playwright and novelist who created Peter Pan.

clue.text: Creator undoes harm in soul

indicators.note: the preposition places one thing within another, so these letters go inside the next piece

parts.note: in Egyptian religion the ba is an aspect of the soul

indicators.note: undoing something takes it apart, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A god reverses the damage done to a person's spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: BA, the Egyptian soul, is a crossword staple; the shuffled HARM sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hinduism Brahma is the creator god, part of the trinity with Vishnu the preserver and Shiva the destroyer.

clue.text: Patrolman on way shows new face

indicators.note: on means placed next to, so pieces sit side by side

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
a ranger patrols a park or forest

explanation.surface: A police officer on his beat shows a different expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New face' looks like a change of expression but means a newcomer.
explanation.definitionFit: A new face is idiom for someone unfamiliar who has just arrived, which is what a stranger is.

clue.text: Criminal presumably able to hold up store

parts.note: a store is a shop
something that lifts, holds things up

explanation.surface: A crook who is apparently capable of robbing a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold up' suggests armed robbery; read literally it means raise, so the criminal is one who could lift a shop. 'Presumably' flags the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoplifter steals goods from stores while posing as a customer, making them a type of thief.

clue.text: Left cuts excellent boxer

indicators.note: to cut into something is to go inside it

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written with I for 1
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A fine boxer's left hand cuts his opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 becomes AI in crosswords because 1 looks like I.
explanation.definitionFit: Muhammad Ali was the three-time world heavyweight champion, perhaps the most famous boxer ever.

clue.text: Evil looks good put next to certain Roman deities

indicators.note: placing side by side joins pieces in sequence

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
the Lares were Roman household gods

explanation.surface: Wicked-looking faces made to seem virtuous beside Roman gods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evil looks good' reads as a moral paradox, but the definition ends at 'looks'.
explanation.definitionFit: A glare is a fierce, angry stare, so glares are hostile looks given in anger.

clue.text: Short message recalled about hospital fundraiser

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters go back the other way
about means around, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: a notelet is a small folded note
H is the abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A brief note remembered about a charity event for a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short message' is a single word, NOTELET, not an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A telethon is a long television broadcast appealing for charitable donations.
